qwen.ref_text: On the battlefield, four players with monster-like strength appeared. Each of the players had already destroyed their colonies. These players were so equally strong, they created a four-way deadlock.

lines: Lecture three. Local search and population search. This is how a search gets stuck on a hill, and how it escapes.
Every evolutionary algorithm repeats the same loop. Here is one lap.
Every EA repeats the same loop.
Score everyone. Here the fitness is the number of ones. Then pick the fitter parents.
Score everyone, then pick the fitter parents.
Next, mix two parents together, and change one gene.
Mix two parents, then change one gene.
Last, the child replaces the weakest. Then the loop repeats.
The child replaces the weakest. Then repeat.
The task is to visit every city once, and then return home.
Visit every city once, then return.
A tour is a string of letters. Add up the hops between cities to get its length.
A tour is a string. Add up the hops.
Shorter is better, so we minimise the length. The length is the fitness.
Shorter is better, so we minimise.
The tour A B C E D has length twenty-eight. That beats the old tour, at thirty-two.
ABCED is shorter: 28 beats 32.
With five cities, there are only twelve different tours.
Five cities have only 12 tours.
Each extra city multiplies the count, first by five, then by six, then by seven.
Each extra city multiplies the count.
With twenty cities there are about sixty quadrillion tours. We cannot check them all.
Twenty cities? We cannot check them all.
Start with one tour, and change it a little to make a mutant.
Start with one tour. Change it a little.
If the mutant is worse, throw the change away.
Worse? Throw the change away.
If it is no worse, keep it, and carry on from there.
No worse? Keep it and carry on.
Repeat this until time runs out.
Repeat until time runs out.
Imagine every solution in a line, side by side. Neighbouring solutions sit next to each other.
Neighbouring solutions sit side by side.
Nearby solutions have similar fitness, so the line forms hills.
Nearby solutions have similar fitness.
Hillclimbing climbs the hill it starts on.
Hillclimbing climbs the hill it starts on.
It stops at a local peak, which may not be the best one.
It stops at a local peak, not the best.
Here are four landscape shapes, with one climber on each. One peak, many peaks, a flat plateau, and a deceptive slope.
Four landscape shapes. One climber on each.
Hillclimbing only ever walks uphill, so it follows whatever slope it finds.
Hillclimbing only ever walks uphill.
Only the one-peak shape always works. The others leave the climber stuck, or heading the wrong way.
Only the one-peak shape always works.
Start from one solution, such as a tour or a string of bits.
Start from one solution.
Every solution that is one mutation away is a neighbour.
Every solution one mutation away is a neighbour.
A different operator gives different neighbours. A swap gives one set, and a bit flip another.
A different operator gives different neighbours.
Hillclimbing is stuck on the small hill on the left.
Hillclimbing is stuck on this hill.
Monte Carlo search, on top, usually rejects a worse step.
A worse step is usually rejected.
Fast-forward, and every worse step is rejected.
Fast-forward: all rejected.
Then one lucky roll of the die lets it step downhill.
One lucky roll: it steps downhill!
From there it climbs on, keeping the best place it has seen.
Then it climbs on, keeping the best.
Below, tabu search always moves to its best neighbour.
Tabu always moves to its best neighbour.
But it may not step back onto a crumb, a place it just left.
But it cannot step back onto a crumb.
So it walks on, down into the valley and across it.
So it walks on, over the valley.
Both methods escape the small hill, and both end on the best peak.
Both can escape the small hill.
A lone hiker climbs the small hill, and is stuck there.
One hiker is stuck on one hill.
Now a team of six starts out on three different hills.
A team starts on many hills.
Even a member with a low score can climb the tallest hill.
A low score can still climb the tallest hill.
The count of hills falls from three to two to one, as the team gathers on the best hill.
The team gathers on the best hill.
A team can also select the fitter members, and recombine them.
A team can select and recombine.
Every evolutionary algorithm runs one loop. Score, pick, change and replace.
Hillclimbing stops on the nearest hill.
To escape, take a step downhill, or send a whole team.
